newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso ends higher at 1,012.60.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso ends higher at 1,012.60.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed 4.4 higher at 1,012.60 after a session that saw the central bank threaten to intervene to halt the local currency's rise against the dollar.

Interbank dealers said the central bank, or Banco de la Republica, flashed an electronic alert across trading screens late in the session, when the peso rose to its intraday high of 1,012.20, saying it intended to buy dollars. There was no sign of any actual dollar-buying by the bank before the close, however, dealers said. The bank has refused to alter the peso's daily floating rate exchange band.

It has come under heavy pressure from the government and leading exporters to halt the peso's rapid appreciation since June, however, when it was trading at 1,074 to the dollar. A stronger peso makes Colombian goods less competitive in the global marketplace and cuts the real value of export earnings.

Colombia's Banking Association said on Thursday that it expects the peso to end the year at 1,005.00 to dollar, a level that would mean a nominal devaluation for the year of just 1.78 percent, well below the government's original target of nearly 14 percent.
The peso's rise Thursday was attributed by one dealer to dollar-sales by two large banks that were apparently short of local currency.
Trading was thin, however, with a total of just $90.4 million in currency changing hands, down from a daily average in recent weeks of about $120 million.
